body:
Full-codebase review, Android finding. Verified by reading.

`AuthRepository.clearLocalSession()` calls `appDb.clearAllTables()`, and it runs on ANY 401 that carried a bearer token (ErrorInterceptor -> SessionEvents -> RootViewModel). Per the wire contract a 401 is also what an idle-expired session and a password change on another device produce — the latter revokes every other session by design. So: edit the list offline on the phone, change the password on the web, foreground the phone -> the whole mirror including the unpushed queue is deleted.

The justification in the comment is that a different account must not see the previous account's lists, but the wipe happens at logout time, before anyone knows which account will log back in.

Fix direction: defer the wipe to login and only wipe when the returning account_id differs, or preserve dirty rows across the clear.
title: Android: a forced logout wipes the local mirror including unpushed edits
